memory_update.text: ULS should be tracked as an underfollowed public TIC gatekeeper for grid, storage, inverter, renewable, transformer and switchgear qualification rather than as a conventional energy stock.
DNOW replaces MRC in the current public universe after the November 2025 DNOW-MRC merger; map DNOW as a low-attention energy/industrial supply-chain assurance and specialty distribution candidate.
The node has two investable sublanes: data/risk platforms such as MCO, and physical procurement-assurance/distribution layers such as WCC and DNOW.
Need deeper evidence on energy-specific revenue contribution for MCO and ULS and scarcity-driven margin/backlog evidence for WCC and DNOW before these candidates can advance beyond Layer 1.

node: Energy supplier-risk intelligence, procurement analytics, inspection, certification, and supply-chain assurance
summary: Expanded the universe for the supplier-risk intelligence/procurement-assurance node. The cleanest public mappings are not pure-play energy companies: Moody's is the reference data/risk platform; UL Solutions is a listed testing/certification gatekeeper for grid, storage, inverter, renewables and utility equipment; WESCO is a large electrical/utility distributor and supply-chain services provider; DNOW is a smaller, more energy-specific distributor with PVF, engineered equipment, digital commerce and supply-chain services across upstream, midstream, gas utilities, downstream, energy transition and industrial markets. D&B would have been relevant but is excluded because it was taken private in August 2025.
